Thanks for the flag. Quick diagnostic and proposal:

1) Root cause (likely): our original invite was created in the organizer's local zone but the .ics omitted an explicit TZID block and used a floating DTSTART/DTEND. When some corporate calendars (esp. Exchange/GCal combinations) import a floating time, they interpret it relative to the recipient's calendar zone and end up shifting by the expected offset. This often shows as an apparent +? hour shift around DST boundaries or when sender/recipient are on opposite sides of the date line.

2) Fix: regenerate the .ics with an explicit VTIMEZONE/TZID (Asia/Tokyo) and include the event DTSTART in local time with TZID, and also include a corresponding UTC DTSTART line. This anchors the invite and prevents floating. Alternatively we can create the event in UTC (e.g., 2027-03-15T17:00:00Z) and mark it as transparent to local calendar clients — but I prefer explicit TZID so attendees see their local label.

3) Immediate action: Vanessa, please create a new event for Mon Mar 15 at 10:00 AM PDT and in the advanced options set the event timezone to America/Los_Angeles. In the event settings add a secondary timezone or include the UTC timestamp in the description. Then "Save and send update". In addition attach the corrected .ics that contains the VTIMEZONE block.

4) Communication: When we resend, include a one-line note for the customer: "We've sent an updated invite that explicitly anchors the event to PST (America/Los_Angeles) with a TZID — please accept the updated invite and let us know if your calendar still shows a discrepancy."

I've attached a sample .ics we use for cross‑region demos (demo-calendar-corrected.ics).
